output.myth: Aun built a boat of cloth and bone and sailed it south, past the last island, because he wanted to see where the wind stopped. The water tilted under him. He kept on until the pole was behind his back and the cold stars were upside down. Mother Hesk saw him go and wound a little more string, and Tavo the Gale came up under the stern and laughed at him. The wind did not let him turn. Aun went all the way round the bottom of the world, and there was his own wake waiting before him, going the same way he was going. Kael still casts for that wake and never catches it. If you see two lamps in the Unflown chasing each other, that is Aun's boat and its trail. Do not wave at them. They are not yet home.
output.verse:
Aun's boat turned for home
its wake kept south past the reef
chasing, not meeting
